 COLUMBIA, S.C. (WACH) — The South Carolina State Election Commission certified the results of the 2026 statewide general election Wednesday, after more than 2 million voters cast ballots.
 According to the commission, 2,054,835 South Carolinians voted in the Nov. 3 election, representing 59.8% of active registered voters.
 RELATED | South Carolina early voting tops 1 million, almost doubles 2022 midterm early votes 
 The commission described the turnout as a historic success for a gubernatorial election year.
 Early voting accounted for the largest share of ballots with 1,043,810 votes cast, or 50.8% of the total.
 Another 966,858 ballots, or 47%, were cast on Election Day, while 44,167 voters, or 2.1%, voted absentee.
 “The 2026 Statewide General Election was a tremendous undertaking, marked by significant voter turnout and commitment of election officials and poll workers across South Carolina,” said the State Election Commission Executive Director, Conway Belangia. Belangia thanked thousands of poll workers and election officials for their work, as well as voters who participated in the election.
 Preparations have begun for the next election cycle, and the commission said that residents should register to vote or update their voter registration information.
 Election results and more information are available at scVOTES.gov.
